# ATS021 — CNPE: Security and Policy Enforcement (Certified Cloud Native Platform Engineer)

[![Liberapay](https://img.shields.io/badge/Liberapay-Support_Astrona.io-F6C915?logo=liberapay&logoColor=black&style=for-the-badge)](https://liberapay.com/Astrona.io)

Course material for the Security and Policy Enforcement domain of the Certified Cloud Native Platform Engineer (CNPE) exam, 15% of the exam. It teaches a platform engineer to lock down a Kubernetes platform from the inside out: least-privilege access with RBAC and Pod Security Admission, mutual TLS and authorization between workloads with Istio and Linkerd, governance with Kyverno, Gatekeeper and ValidatingAdmissionPolicy, audit trails and compliance evidence (API server audit logs, Kyverno policy reports and Gatekeeper audit results), and compliance gates in a Tekton delivery pipeline plus admission-time image policies. Every change is proved on a live kind cluster by an admission decision or a real request.

This course covers the **Security and Policy Enforcement** domain of the Certified Cloud Native Platform Engineer (CNPE) exam, **15% of the exam**.

Everything lives under `sections/`. Each section is a set of modules, and each module is:

- a **landing page** (`course.md`) plus, where the subject needs it, ordered **deep-dive parts** (`course-0N-*.md`), woven with hands-on "Try it" checkpoints and Mermaid diagrams;
- an ungraded **playground** — a throwaway environment to explore in;

Each section ends with a **capstone lab** combining its modules and a knowledge-check quiz.

[`astrona.yaml`](astrona.yaml) is the manifest: every section, module, reading, playground, lab and capstone in the order they are meant to be taken.

Everything targets **kind v0.33.0**, **kind_node_image kindest/node:v1.35.8**, **istio 1.31.1**, **linkerd edge-26.10.1**, **kyverno 1.19.1**, **gatekeeper 3.23.1**, **cert-manager 1.21.2**, **tekton-pipelines 1.17.0**, **tkn 0.46.1**, **kyverno-cli-image ghcr.io/kyverno/kyverno-cli:v1.19.1**, **podinfo 6.15.0**, **go-httpbin 2.25.0** on `kind`.

## How to work through it

1. Open the section's `README.md` for the map.
2. Read each module's `course.md`, then its deep-dive parts in order.
3. Boot the module playground and run the "Try it" checkpoints alongside the text.
4. Solve the section capstone without looking at the walkthrough.
5. Take the section quiz, then the final domain quiz once every section is done.
